name: OET-LV
scope: Explicit 83-book OET-LV source profile: 66 core books, 14 Brenton DC books, native PSS/ODE Swete addresses, and Latin LAO with reviewed reference boundaries. Earlier reviewed mappings and unresolved intervals are retained. LAO 1:1-20 maps individually to the BOS reference; this does not claim identical textual readings.

evidence.method: LV OT follows original numbering; LV NT follows VLT, including the Philippians 1:16-17 order. Native word references are unchanged.
evidence.attribution: OT definitions use Copenhagen Alliance data and the BOS supplement (CC BY-SA 4.0); see source-manifest.json. NT uses the reviewed VLT and BibleTagsNT boundaries.

additionalBooksReview.scope: Native address inventory only; not a versification alignment or approval of the lexical draft text.
additionalBooksReview.method: Inventory every chapter and verse marker from the two generated ESFM files, preserving missing labels and exact a/b suffixes. Compare against the bundled Copenhagen counts and OET source-assembly documentation. Counts establish native addresses, not equivalent reference passages.
additionalBooksReview.sourceEdition: H. B. Swete, The Old Testament in Greek, volume III (1905), via Open Greek and Latin / First1KGreek.

upstreamSources.attribution: Open Greek and Latin / First1KGreek; Harvard College Library; Digital Divide Data transcription of H. B. Swete, The Old Testament in Greek, volume III (1905)
Open Greek and Latin / First1KGreek; Harvard College Library; Digital Divide Data transcription of H. B. Swete, The Old Testament in Greek, volume III (1905)

additionalBooksReview.attribution: Native labels derive from Open Greek and Latin / First1KGreek; Harvard College Library; Digital Divide Data transcription of Swete, CC BY-SA 4.0. OET assembly changes are documented in scripts/DC/README.md. Copenhagen reference counts are attributed in the BOS source-manifest.json. No Bible text or lexical data is copied here.
notes: BOS ODE is USFM ODA, Biblical Odes, not Odes of Solomon. PSS is Psalms of Solomon, not Psalm 151 (PS2). Both book identities already exist in BOSReference.

ODE 4 combines two source songs, iva (Isaiah 5) and ivb (Isaiah 26). Native labels are 1a-9a followed by 9b-20b. These suffixes are source distinctions, not a claim that reference verse 9 is split in the same way.
ODE 14:1-47 are local XML poetry-line ordinals, not conventional verse numbers; do not map them positionally to the 46-verse reference chapter.
ODE 10 preserves source order 68,71,72,69,70,73; profile counts do not reorder stored text. Native callers can request explicit ordered references.
ODE 7:15 and 13:74 are missing source divisions. Other excluded labels precede the numbered song extracts. None implies that the corresponding reference text is absent.
No identityBooks entries or mappedVerses are added for these books. unsupportedBooks blocks both conversion directions, including apparently matching early verses.
The OET ESFM/XML files are evidence only, never runtime or test dependencies. The other 14 LV DC drafts are reviewed separately in evidence.deuterocanonicalReview.

deuterocanonicalReview.method: Inventory native ESFM labels; compare the retained Brenton Greek words with the Greek reference boundary witnesses and reviewed RV passages. Preserve chapter transpositions, lettered whole-verse aggregates and complete split/merge groups. Textual variants do not imply word-for-word equivalence. All definitions are bundled and reference-directed; no source checkout or automatic text matching is used at runtime.

notes: BAR 6 is assembled from the Brenton Letter of Jeremiah; its boundaries differ from RV even where their chapter maxima match.
SIR 30-36 transposes sections. LV 36:16 contains both reference 33:16a and 36:10b; its complete group also requires LV 30:25-26 and 33:11.

An unsuffixed native verse denotes all stored entries with that number, including its suffixes. Explicit suffixes validate natively but have no independent cross-system mapping unless declared. Do not assign a suffix to the following numbered verse by guesswork.
ESG additions (1:1, 3:13, 4:17-47 RV / 4:17 LV, 5:1-2, 8:12, 10:3-14 RV / 10:3 LV), DNG 1-12, and TOB 13:6-10 RV / 13:6-7 LV remain unreviewed reference bridges. These are unknown, not absent text.
LES has no LV source file. PSS and ODE remain separately inventoried and unsupported for cross-system mapping.

The pinned Copenhagen files and reference catalogue are unchanged. Copenhagen attribution and CC BY-SA 4.0 license are recorded in source-manifest.json. No Bible text or lexical glosses are copied into this profile.

unresolvedRanges.ESG 1:1; 3:13; 4:17; 5:1-2; 8:12; 10:3: Integrated additions require a reviewed reference segment convention. Ordinary intervals are explicitly mapped; no whole-book identity is declared.
unresolvedRanges.DNG 1-12: The provisional reference composite remains unresolved. Mapping these chapters to Hebrew DAN would introduce duplicate candidates within this profile. Chapters 13-14 are explicitly mapped to SUS/BEL instead.
unresolvedRanges.TOB 13:6-7: The full reference passage around the Greek witness lacuna is not verified. The Brenton/RV correspondence alone cannot establish the missing reference boundaries. No identity fallback or assertion of absent text is made.

laodiceansReview.method: Compared the actual 20 ESFM verses, Lightfoot Latin (1875, pp. 353-355), James English (1924, pp. 478-479), and the numbered English boundary witness used by BOS reference-policy LAO. All 20 numbered passage boundaries correspond individually. This is a passage-address review, not an assertion of identical readings or approval of the draft translation.

boundaryConvention.1-14: Greeting, thanks, warning, work, bonds, salvation, living/dying, unity, obedience, God at work, action, rejoicing, requests: each passage stays within its corresponding numbered verse.
boundaryConvention.15: Complete list of qualities and instruction to do them.
boundaryConvention.16: Retain what was heard and received.
boundaryConvention.17: Peace. This is the final clause of printed Lightfoot 16, explicitly split by the OET importer.

laodiceansReview.limits: Wycliffe-Zefania 15-16 remains an atomic group when converting to/from OET. No holy-kiss greeting is substituted for verse 17. Neither a common 20-verse count nor this review certifies every Latin witness. Individual word alignment is outside this profile.
laodiceansReview.attribution: Lightfoot and James are public-domain editions. OET text is CC BY-SA 4.0. The Marlowe rendering was consulted only to compare boundaries with the existing BOS convention; no copyrighted translation text is bundled. This address review uses the profile CC-BY-SA-4.0 licence.

unsupportedBooks.PSS: OET-LV retains the Swete/First1KGreek source numbering, which differs from the Copenhagen org reference. The 18 Psalms have 332 native verse labels versus 293 in the reference. Native/same-system access is supported; no cross-system mapping is asserted until the source boundaries are reviewed. This is an unresolved alignment, not absent text.
unsupportedBooks.ODE: OET-LV retains the Swete/First1KGreek source numbering, which differs from the Copenhagen org reference. Odes have a different chapter arrangement, sparse labels, separate songs encoded with a/b suffixes, and 47 local XML-line labels in chapter 14. Native/same-system access is supported; no cross-system mapping is asserted until the source boundaries are reviewed. This is an unresolved alignment, not absent text.
